authorial_core.source_request: 시각 의미 데이터와 후보 데이터에 반영해줘. 그 다음 스킬의 최신 버전을 사용하여 독립된 서브에이전트 3개에서 각각 서로 다른 컨셉으로 이번에 반영한 주제가 이미지에 실제로 반영되는지까지 테스트할 수 있는 주제에 어울리는 랜덤한 컨셉을 정하여 테스트케이스를 마련하고 첨부한 이미지를 활용하여 프롬프트 작성하고 이미지 생성하도록 하여 잘 반영되었는지 테스트해줘.
authorial_core.interpreted_intent: The requester asks for independent random concepts that test the newly integrated topic with the attached image. The exact prior-user topic in the coordinator envelope identifies medical horror; it supplies a genre, not a prescribed patient history. This arm independently chooses the fictional after-hours discharge counter: the woman receives an empty sleeve while her record remains beyond glass and the exit is bolted. I compared an automatically repeating wristband printer and a file observed through archive glass; the empty-sleeve encounter gives a tangible failed exchange and a readable barrier at creativity 1. Every role, wardrobe, door bolt, prop, gesture, and staging decision is authorial and replaceable. Only facial appearance and short hair are taken from the supplied portrait; the image establishes no biography, actual medical condition, age, consent, wardrobe, or inner life. The user prescribed neither clothing, exposure, nor age. Sensual 1 subtly supports the woman's distinct presence through intimate warm light and unguarded stillness; fetish 0 adds no erotic focus, surreal 0 keeps the hospital plausible, and no explicit-nonsexual override was inferred. WHO: a fictional visitor who wants her record and release. WHERE: an unstaffed discharge counter where glass blocks the returned exchange. HOW: the viewer shares her side of that barrier. WHY NOW: the sleeve has just come back empty and her fingers have not yet left the closed hatch. The frame should read first as a person stranded by ordinary institutional mechanisms, with the evidence of withholding close enough to understand at one glance.
authorial_core.subject: A fictional woman based on the supplied portrait for face and short hair appearance only.
authorial_core.setting: An after-hours hospital discharge records counter and the adjacent closed exit.
authorial_core.event: She receives an empty records sleeve and sees her chart retained behind security glass.
visual_priorities: The human face and paused hands on the patient side establish the immediate failed exchange.
The empty sleeve, closed transfer hatch, and visible chart on the staff side make the medical record inaccessible in the same view.
The nearby bolted exit and empty clinical corridor turn discharge into institutional confinement.
A small warm light on the woman separates her intimate presence from the cool hospital geometry.
authorial_core.baseline_prompt_en: A fictional clinical encounter charged with dread, photographed as a grounded hospital scene. The central figure is a reference-inspired woman, preserving the supplied portrait's facial appearance and short dark bob with a light, separated fringe. She stands at the after-hours discharge records counter in a charcoal sleeveless jersey top and pale trousers, wearing a narrow hospital identification band. She has just been handed an empty transparent record sleeve. Her left hand holds its open mouth against the counter; the fingers of her right hand remain on the metal lip of the now-closed transfer hatch. Through the clear lower portion of the security glass, her thick chart rests on the staff side, close enough to see yet physically beyond her reach. The small portrait clipped to that chart repeats her face. Her eyes are fixed on this inaccessible file, her lips slightly parted and her shoulders held still; a soft amber desk lamp catches her cheek and bare forearm, giving her an intimate human presence against the building's indifferent surfaces. Immediately beyond her, a closed hospital exit door has a plainly visible steel sliding bolt across its seam. The waiting seats are empty, a queue dispenser hangs idle, and the long corridor of numbered clinical doors leads into fluorescent distance. The viewer stands beside the patient side of the counter at her eye level, close enough to understand the empty sleeve and her interrupted gesture while keeping the chart, glass barrier, and bolted exit legible in the same horizontal frame. Restrained color photography, cool green-white institutional light, one small amber pool, mild grain, real worn laminate and rubbed stainless steel. The frightening event is the hospital retaining control of her record after the ordinary promise of discharge; her living, particular presence meets a system that has stopped responding.
